record.paper_title: Status, open problems and prospects of the decay B+ → ℓ+νℓ
record.original_question: Can more precise measurements of the branching ratio for the purely leptonic decay B+ → τ+ντ resolve the tension between the experimental average (1.64 ± 0.34) × 10−4 and indirect CKM global-fit determinations, where CKMfitter places the indirect determination 2.6 standard deviations from the experimental value and UTfit places it 3.2 standard deviations away?

evidence.quote: In contrast, the B+ → τ+ντ channel is a well established decay, with a value (1.64±0.34)×10−4 (combining all the experimental findings [5]), which is in agreement with the SM expectation. However, this last experimental result is a source of tension within the the CKM global fit. The indirect determination of B+ → τ+ντ turns out to be at 2.6σ ( 3.2σ) from the experimental value, as estimated by the CKMfitter [9] (UTfit [10]) collaboration. More precise experimental findings are needed to disentangle the current state of affairs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the purely leptonic decay $B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau$ has a branching ratio that can be predicted indirectly from a global fit to the parameters of the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) quark-mixing matrix (using inputs such as $|V_{ub}|$, the $B$-meson decay constant $f_B$, the $B$-meson lifetime, and the unitarity-triangle constraints), and can also be measured directly in $B$-factory experiments. The current world-average direct experimental measurement is
$$\mathcal{B}(B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau)_{\text{exp}} = (1.64 \pm 0.34) \times 10^{-4},$$
while the indirect global-fit determinations disagree with this value at the level of $2.6\sigma$ (CKMfitter-style fit) and $3.2\sigma$ (UTfit-style fit).

Question: Will future, more precise experimental measurements of $\mathcal{B}(B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau)$ resolve this tension between the direct measurement and the indirect CKM global-fit determination — that is, will the discrepancy converge toward zero (consistent with the Standard Model fit) or persist/grow into a significant deviation indicative of physics beyond the Standard Model?
artifact.category_tag: CKM unitarity and rare B-meson decays
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent measurements (notably the 2015 Belle semileptonic-tag analysis with the full Belle dataset) brought the experimental branching ratio closer to the Standard Model CKM-fit prediction, substantially reducing the previously reported 2.6–3.2σ tension. However, the precision is still limited and the program of improving this measurement (e.g., Belle II and proposed FCC-ee studies) remains active, so the question of definitively resolving the tension is not fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the branching fraction of B+ → τ+ ν_τ decays with the semileptonic tagging method and the full Belle data sample
status_evidence.snippet: Belle's full-data semileptonic-tag measurement of B+ → τ+ν refined the branching ratio and reduced the tension with the CKM global fit.
status_evidence.claim: Updated experimental measurements have reduced the previously reported tension.

status_evidence.title: Prospects for B_c+ and B+ → τ+ ν_τ at FCC-ee
status_evidence.snippet: Prospects for precise measurements of the purely leptonic B+ → τ+ν_τ branching ratio at FCC-ee, proposed as a novel determination of |V_ub|.
status_evidence.claim: Improved precision is still being pursued, indicating the question is not fully resolved.
